LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 HAND WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we write words and sentences neatly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  look at samples of texts with good handwriting,  Identify aspects of good handwriting. Learners with speech difficulties can identify orally, by typing or writing

2. In purposive groups, copy letter patterns of words with the target letter-sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘thr’), with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.

3. Listen to a dictation on verbs in the present and past tense and write them. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology to write.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  look at samples of texts with good handwriting,  Identify aspects of good handwriting. Learners with speech difficulties can identify orally, by typing or writing
2. In purposive groups, copy letter patterns of words with the target letter-sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘thr’), with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.
3. Listen to a dictation on verbs in the present and past tense and write them. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology to write.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is enhanced as they write words in clear and legible

handwriting.

 Digital literacy: The learner’s ability to create with technology is improved as they type words and phrases on digital

devices.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates the effort of peers to write correctly and assist those with writing difficulties.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner Support Programmes (Peer Education and Mentorship): The learner’s ability to mentor others is developed as they

model good handwriting to their peers.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses the handwriting skills to learn similar concept in Kiswahili Language Activities.
